course.description: Build a reusable Cowork task that maintains your fixed asset register, calculates depreciation using straight-line or declining balance methods, and processes disposals with gain/loss — updated and accurate every period.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Set Up the Depreciation Scheduler Skill in Claude Cowork.

lessons.content:
The **Depreciation Scheduler** skill is a saved Cowork task that maintains your fixed asset register, runs depreciation calculations each period, and handles disposals — keeping your schedule accurate without manual spreadsheet work.

**What it handles:**
- Maintains a running fixed asset register with asset details, acquisition dates, and useful lives
- Calculates depreciation using straight-line or declining balance method (or both)
- Processes asset disposals: calculates net book value, proceeds, and gain/loss on disposal
- Outputs an updated depreciation schedule and journal entry figures for the period

**Why build it as a skill:** Depreciation runs every period on the same assets — set the rules once and update only when assets are added or disposed.
lessons.title: What this skill does

lessons.content:
1. Open **Claude Cowork** on your desktop
2. Click **New Task**
3. Name it: **Depreciation Scheduler**
4. Leave the task open — the next step is where you write the instructions that make this a real skill

> **Note:** In Cowork, a "skill" is simply a task with good instructions. The name you give it is what you'll see every time you open it. Keep it short and descriptive — "Depreciation Scheduler" is perfect.
lessons.title: Create the task in Cowork

activities.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

lessons.content:
In the task instructions field, paste the prompt below. **Replace the depreciation methods, useful lives, and disposal rules with your firm's accounting policy.**

---

*"You are my Depreciation Scheduler. I will maintain a fixed asset register with you. Each period, I will tell you: (a) any new assets acquired, (b) any assets disposed of, and (c) the current period end date.*

*Apply the following rules — replace with your firm's actual accounting policy:*

*Depreciation methods:*
- *Buildings: Straight-line over 40 years → Replace with your useful life*
- *Plant & equipment: Declining balance at 25% → Replace with your rate*
- *Motor vehicles: Straight-line over 5 years → Replace with your useful life*
- *Computer equipment: Straight-line over 3 years → Replace with your useful life*
- *Intangibles: Straight-line over useful life as specified at acquisition*

*For each asset, maintain:*
- *Asset ID, description, acquisition date, cost, accumulated depreciation, net book value*

*For new acquisitions: add to the register and calculate depreciation from acquisition date (or start of period — specify your policy)*

*For disposals: calculate NBV at disposal date, compare to proceeds, calculate gain or loss on disposal*

*Each period, output:*
- *Updated asset register (full)*
- *Depreciation charge for the period by asset class*
- *Journal entry figures: Debit Depreciation Expense, Credit Accumulated Depreciation*
- *Disposal entries if applicable: Debit Proceeds, Credit Asset Cost, Debit/Credit Accumulated Depreciation, Debit/Credit Gain/Loss on Disposal"*

---

> **Make it yours:** Paste in your full asset register on first run. Include your GL account codes so journal entries come out ready to post.

activities.title: Run it and save your skill

lessons.content:
# Run it and save your skill

You've built the task — now run it and lock it in.

## Run your first depreciation schedule

1. Open Cowork and navigate to your **Depreciation Scheduler** task
2. Attach a sample fixed asset register (spreadsheet or paste the data directly)
3. Hit **Run** and review the output:
   - Does it correctly calculate straight-line or declining balance?
   - Are disposals handled with gain/loss?
   - Is the output formatted in a way you can drop into your workpapers?

## If something's off

Edit the task instructions — be more specific about:
- The exact depreciation method(s) you use
- How you want disposals presented
- The output format (table, CSV, narrative)

Re-run until the output matches your standard.

## Save it as a reusable skill

Once you're happy with the output:
- **Rename the task** to something clear: e.g. `Depreciation Scheduler — Straight-Line`
- Pin it or star it so it's easy to find each period
- If you handle multiple methods, clone the task and adjust for each variant

## You now have a repeatable process

Every period: open the task, drop in the asset register, get your schedule. No manual recalculation. No formatting from scratch.
